findings.title: #124's new refill arm is never exercised by any golden — health_recover heals via the pre-existing all-clear recharge, and the PR tuning table cites that demo as meter_refill_per_tick's measured effect
findings.evidence: Mutation-proof (Perkins): meter_refill_streak_ticks 200->1000000 leaves health_recover behaviorally identical (min 40 -> 100, score 49). Code path: in-grace (ticks 84-984) the meter sits at 100 (the arm needs <100); ticks 984-1013 drain (streak resets); after 1013 !any_breach routes healing to the unchanged recharge branch. PR body: '| `meter_refill_per_tick` | — (no path) | **1** | scarred meter heals +1%/tick once no drain is active (health_recover: trough 40 → 100) |'.
findings.detail: The #124 mechanic is real (unit-pinned, mutation-verified RED when disabled) but ships unit-test-only; the golden named as its demonstration does not execute it, and the tuning-table row over-credits the new knob. Acceptance criterion '(2) a real recovery path exists and is demonstrated in a golden' is met for the recovery LOOP (which is genuinely new end-to-end: pre-fix the same run dies at 533) but the new arm itself has no golden.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend health_recover (or add a sibling golden) where a second class stays breach-latched-in-grace with meter <100 so the +1/tick in-grace refill visibly drives the heal; re-cite the tuning-table row to that demonstration (or disclose unit-pin-only).

findings.title: health_recover.dem misdescribes its own timeline: the fix lands at 40.0 s, the drain starts at 49.2 s — the fight-back happens inside the grace, not 'mid-drain', deviating from the frozen spec sequence committed in this same PR
findings.evidence: Demo: 'The fix ... lands at 40 s' (at 40000ms demolish pipe 0) and 'the player FIGHTS BACK inside the drain'. PR body: 'the player fights back mid-drain'. Measured stats: drain starts tick 984 (49.2 s). Frozen spec line 51: 'narrow-path saturation → Grace_Expired → meter mid-drain → demolish+wide-fan fix → breach exits → meter refills to 100'.
findings.detail: The implemented sequence is fix (40 s) → grace expires (49.2 s) → drain → trough → all-clear heal: the spec's mid-drain-fix order is inverted and the heal arm differs; header and PR body still tell the mid-drain story.
findings.recommended_fix: Re-time the fix past 49.2 s to match the spec sequence (which would also let the trough demonstrate the refill arm — see W1), or correct the spec's Code Map line and the header/PR wording to the measured order.

findings.title: era3_surge_survivable.dem header claims 'Pre-fix (grace 400) this exact mesh DIED at ~57 s' — false by mutation experiment: under grace 400 the same demo wins identically (score 213, meter 100, tick 3000)

findings.title: New balance keys parsed with lenient jint (silent float truncation, i32 wrap) where jint_strict exists — consistent with all sibling health keys
findings.detail: jint truncates 2.5 -> 2 and wraps out-of-i32-range through the cast; the >=1 validation cannot catch in-range wrong values. Sibling health keys share the pattern, so this is doctrine hygiene, not a regression.
findings.recommended_fix: Migrate the health block to jint_strict in a follow-up.
